_doc: Street-grid block fill: grid block r3c4, measured at 31% sprite coverage. Its west neighbour r3c3 just became parkland (d31), so this one is BUILT — two facing terraces — to stop the whole southern band turning into one continuous green swathe. NOTE the bbox is 672x576, not 768x624: a road crosses at world x3296-4096 y2992-3056, the d5 district spills in from local x680 (mailboxes, info boards, police box), and the park/graveyard/camping band already occupies local y592+ where the big grass patch starts at world y3200. Compile: python3 scripts/compile-exterior-district.py --spec data/city-specs/biome-specs/blocks/d33-midtown-terrace.json --qa -v. See d29-midtown-retail.json's _layout_doc for the 16px-lattice and 16px-halo rules.
label: MIDTOWN TERRACE

surfaces.name: front_gardens
surfaces._doc: planting strip between the two terraces; the south row's sprites start at y320 so nothing is buried

landmarks._doc: north terrace, 160x240 => y16-256. No two adjacent houses share a design: terraced_house_3 and _5 are both grey corrugated and read as the SAME building side by side, which made the first cut look copy-pasted.
south terrace fronting the arterial. 288x256 balconied house => y304-560; a different massing from the north row so the two sides of the garden strip don't mirror each other.

slots.name: garden_strip
slots._doc: decor_small kept light: residential.forbid_tags covers military/grave/worksite/subway but NOT camping, so a heavier scatter pulls in camp furniture

keep_clear.why: north kerb band: d00 traffic light + planters stand here
south kerb stays walkable; the park/graveyard band begins just below at world y3200

constraints._doc: 42x36 tiles = 1512 cells. Five house shells (three 160-192px north, a 288px country house plus one terrace south) claim most of the solid budget by design.
